assertions.description: The frame-sizing property accepts the content-height keyword.
The frame-sizing property accepts the content-width keyword.
The frame-sizing property accepts the logical content-block-size keyword.
The frame-sizing property accepts the logical content-inline-size keyword.
The frame-sizing property accepts its initial value, auto.
The frame-sizing grammar is keyword-only: a length like 100px must NOT parse (also vacuously true where the property is entirely unsupported).
frame-sizing set on an iframe element round-trips through getComputedStyle as the specified keyword.
assertions.test: (() => { const f = document.createElement('iframe'); f.style.setProperty('frame-sizing', 'content-height'); f.setAttribute('title', 'conformance probe frame'); document.body.appendChild(f); const v = getComputedStyle(f).getPropertyValue('frame-sizing').trim(); f.remove(); return v === 'content-height'; })()

assertions.description: The Window interface exposes the requestResize() method.
Calling window.requestResize() from a top-level window (not a child navigable) throws a NotAllowedError DOMException. Fails honestly where the method is missing.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof window.requestResize !== 'function') return false; try { window.requestResize(); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof DOMException && e.name === 'NotAllowedError'; } })()
